thread:
lucas: FYI customer 'ACME' reports ~30k missing audit events in the webhook forwarder -> their Splunk HEC endpoint. They also see intermittent 403s. Sample logs + repro below.

lucas: repro steps:
1) create cert rotation and webhook target configured as https://siem-acme.example.com/hec
2) forwarder mode = webhook-push, schema = v2, gzip=true
3) after our KMS alias rotation window (09:02-09:05 UTC) they see 403s and later missing tenant_id on ~10% of events

lucas: key snippets from forwarder logs (redacted):
```
2026-03-16T09:03:12Z WARN forwarder.http deliver failed status=403 url=/hec x-rdwd-keyid=alias/rdw-2026-rot1 x-rdwd-signature=sha256:ABCD... reason="signature-mismatch"
2026-03-16T09:03:29Z INFO forwarder.replay queued 12 events for retry tenant=acme-42
2026-03-16T09:04:01Z INFO forwarder.http deliver status=200 url=/hec x-rdwd-keyid=alias/rdw-2026-rot2 x-rdwd-signature=sha256:EFGH...
2026-03-16T09:05:30Z INFO forwarder.batch sent 0 events (gzipped payload length mismatch)
```

lucas: They attached SIEM side logs that show HEC rejecting with "signature invalid" and some events arriving with schema_v=1 fields (no tenant_id).

maya: thanks, lucas. Are they on the managed forwarder (v2.3.1) or a private forwarder? Also did they rotate their HEC token around that time?

lucas: managed v2.3.1. No token rotation on their side. We rotated KMS alias on our end for envelope signing (scheduled rotation).

tim: quick hypothesis: during KMS alias rotation we briefly produced signatures with the new key id but some cached worker processes still used the pre-rotation signer or had stale key metadata, producing mixed x-rdwd-keyid headers. Combined with gzip chunk size changes that changed Content-Length calculation, the SIEM rejects some batches and stores partial events without tenant_id (we saw a fallback path that strips v2 fields on parse error).

tim: can you paste the raw HTTP headers of a failed request (from forwarder logs)? I want to confirm x-rdwd-signature/x-rdwd-keyid vs payload CRC.

lucas: pasted snippet from payload queue:
```
POST /hec HTTP/1.1
Host: siem-acme.example.com
Content-Encoding: gzip
Content-Length: 18243
X-RDWD-SIGNATURE: sha256:ABCD1234
X-RDWD-KEYID: alias/rdw-2026-rot1
X-RDWD-SCHEMA-VER: 2

(binary gzipped body...)
```

maya: noted. If tim's hypothesis is right, temporary mitigation is to disable signature validation for that customer route (internal flag) while we backfill. That will stop 403s but we still need to re-send the missing events.

tim: agreed. Mitigation steps I recommend:
- set route.validate_signature = false for tenant acme-42 (console or CLI)
- run replayer for timeframe 2026-03-16T09:00 -> 2026-03-16T09:10 with strict ordering to avoid duplicates
- run a small canary replay to their HEC with a single gzipped batch to confirm acceptance

tim: replay command (internal tools):
```
replayer --tenant acme-42 --from 2026-03-16T09:00Z --to 2026-03-16T09:10Z --target webhook --dry-run=false --batch-size=1000
```

lucas: toggled validate_signature=false at 09:20. 403s dropped immediately, but customer still reports ~3k missing events. They want backfill timeline and assurance about schema integrity.

maya: two questions for eng-sec: 1) was there a known bug in 2.3.1 around signature key cache or gzip length calc? 2) if we replay, do we need to rewrite the signature headers or send unsigned batches?

tim: short answers: 1) there is an existing race in signer cache that can surface during alias rotation (we'll link the bug). 2) if validate_signature=false on their route, we can replay unsigned (the replayer has --omit-signature) or sign with the current key id. Prefer unsigned to match mitigation and avoid another mismatch.

tim: I'll open INC-5421 for the signer race and tag it P0 for a patch. Workaround docs: https://internal.redwood.example.com/playbooks/audit-webhook-backfill (internal).

deploy-bot: deploy finished: forwarder v2.3.2 candidate rolled to canary at 2026-03-16T10:05 UTC (includes signer-cache fix).

lucas: good to know. Customer asked about forensic evidence: can we produce a list of event_ids that were accepted vs dropped during the window?

maya: we can produce a delta by comparing journal sequences vs successful delivery logs. I'll produce an initial CSV and share. ETA 2h.

tim: action items:
- (tim) open INC-5421 + link to logs + owner (in progress)
- (maya) generate delivery delta CSV and coordinate replay windows with customer (ETA 2h)
- (lucas) confirm whether customer wants unsigned replays or signed once route is toggled
- (infra) watch for further 403s after canary v2.3.2 roll (deployed to canary)

lucas: thanks all. I'll wait for CSV and then approve replay.

maya: assigning on the thread: maya -> coordinate with customer, tim -> eng fix, infra -> monitor canary. :thumbsup:
